Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Los Angeles/Oxnard CA 
352 PM PST Fri Nov 27 2026

.SYNOPSIS...27/112 PM.

A cooling trend will begin Saturday as the first in a series of
storms move through the region. The first chance for rain will be
Sunday afternoon, with off and on rain, very heavy at times, 
through at least Wednesday morning.

&&

.SHORT TERM (TDY-MON)...27/136 PM.

Another warm fall day across southern California with highs mostly
in the low to mid 80s for coast and coastal valleys courtesy of
moderate offshore gradients along with 500mb heights around 590dam
which are over the 95th percentile for this time of year. Not
quite breaking daily temperature records but a few areas got
close. 

Coast and coastal valley temperatures will drop off sharply this 
weekend as onshore flow returns and the massive ridge gets pushed
to the east by the next storm system. Most of those areas will
cool off by 4-8 degrees each of the next two days, bringing highs
back down to normal or even a little below normal by Sunday and
Monday. Interior areas, as usual after a Santa Ana, will either
warm slightly or remain about the same this weekend then cool
Monday as next system moves in.

Speaking of which, the first in a series of storms will be moving
into the Central Coast as early as Sunday afternoon with some 
light scattered showers. Those will make their way south Sunday
night into Monday morning. Amounts in most areas through Monday
afternoon are expected to be under a quarter inch, except as much
as a half inch along the Central Coast.

.LONG TERM (TUE-FRI)...27/237 PM.

No big changes in the forecast for the primary storm next week,
which now seems to begin as early as Monday night. Models are in
very good agreement showing the upper low crossing 140w close to
36 degrees north latitude which is much farther south than usual
and sets up a track towards southern California that is
climatologically favored to produce severe weather, especially in
LA County. This track will also cross over SSTs that are still
5-10 degrees above normal. So it's not surprising that many of the
ensemble solutions increased rain amounts, particularly on 
Tuesday when there is at least a 20-30 percent chance of rain 
rates reaching or exceeding 1 inch per hour in the upslope areas 
south of Point Conception. 

As we've been emphasizing, residents, especially in areas that 
are compromised by fires in the last year or two should pay close 
attention to the forecasts and begin preparations to protect your
property. Also, make plans now for possible evacuations

A little ridge will bring dry conditions to the area on Thursday
with a weak likely inconsequential system still slated for 
Friday.

&&

.AVIATION...27/2351Z.

At 2330Z at KLAX, there was a surface-based inversion. The top of
the inversion was at 1500 feet with a temp of 24 deg C.

High confidence in the 00Z TAFs with VFR conds expected at all 
the airfields thru the fcst period.

KLAX...High confidence in VFR TAF. Good confidence that any east 
wind component remains below 7 kts.

KBUR...High confidence in VFR TAF.

&&

.MARINE...27/203 PM.

For the Outer Waters, moderate to high confidence in current 
forecast. Expecting Small Craft Advisory (SCA) level seas with 
areas of SCA level winds to persist through tonight. Then conds 
will be largely below SCA levels Saturday through Monday before 
seas increase Monday night to SCA levels ahead of an approaching 
strong storm system. Winds are expected to increase to SCA to Gale
Force Tuesday and continue through Tuesday night along with large
and increasingly hazardous seas as the storm impacts the area. SCA
winds and seas will continue Wednesday and Wednesday night, with a
50% chance of Gale Force winds at times on Wednesday.

For the Inner Waters north of Point Sal, moderate to high confidence
in current forecast. Expecting SCA level winds and seas to linger
through late tonight. Conds will be largely below SCA levels 
Saturday through Monday evening before winds increase late Monday
night to SCA levels ahead of an approaching strong storm system. 
Winds are expected to increase further to Gale Force Tuesday as 
the storm impacts the area. Winds and seas to SCA levels can be
expected Tuesday night, with seas to SCA levels persisting
Wednesday and Wednesday night.

For the Inner Waters south of Point Conception, moderate to high
confidence in current forecast. Today through Monday evening, 
winds and seas are expected to remain below SCA. Winds are 
expected to increase to SCA levels Monday night ahead of an 
approaching strong storm system. Gale Force winds are expected 
Tuesday and Tuesday night as the storm impacts the region. Winds
to SCA levels are expected for the southern waters Wednesday, 
otherwise conds should be below SCA levels Wednesday and 
Wednesday night.

It looks more and more likely there will be significant impacts
over the coastal waters from the Pacific storm system forecast 
mainly from Monday night into Tuesday evening. Strong Gale Force
winds and hazardous seas will spread to all the coastal waters
with this system, along with the potential for squalls with 
thunderstorms and waterspouts. Poor visibility in heavy rain is 
also expected. Mariners are encouraged to pay close attention to 
the latest forecasts and any future statements regarding this 
storm system.

&&

.BEACHES...27/202 PM.

A large, long period, west swell will continue to slowly subside
across the waters. High surf will continue through Saturday 
across the Central Coast from Point Conception northward, as well 
as the Los Angeles County coast. There will be many, strong rip 
currently nearly everywhere, strong long shore currents, some risk
of sneaker waves, large shore pound, and coastal erosion. These 
conditions will lead to an increased risk of drowning and make 
swimming dangerous.

In addition, an exceptionally high tide of up to 7.2 feet is 
predicted for Saturday morning, and this will continue the threat 
of minor to moderate coastal flooding over low-lying coastal 
areas. A Coastal Flood Advisory continues until 2 PM Saturday for 
the Ventura County beaches. Elsewhere, low-lying coastal areas 
with no protection from the ocean will still be vulnerable to sea
water intrusion during the Saturday morning high tide.

Please check out LAXCFWLOX for the latest details about all of the
current advisories in effect.
